title: Faster approximate dynamic distances on monotone grids
formal: For an \(N\)-vertex directed grid with east, north and northeast arcs and nonnegative weights, can opposite-corner distance be maintained within \(1+\varepsilon\) using \(\operatorname{polylog}(N)\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon)\) update time and \(\sqrt N\operatorname{polylog}(N)\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon)\) query time, with polynomial preprocessing and an offline-known update sequence?

import_provenance.original_title: Faster approximate dynamic distances on monotone grids
import_provenance.original_statement: For a directed N-vertex grid with east, north and northeast arcs and nonnegative weights, can fixed opposite-corner distances be maintained within 1+ε with polylog(N)·poly(1/ε) update time and √N polylog(N)·poly(1/ε) query time? Allow polynomial preprocessing and an offline-known sequence of arbitrary weight changes.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Editorial benchmark sharpening the paper’s explicit dynamic-grid question; its reduction would yield near-quadratic approximate DTW under translation. Approximation is essential here: exact dynamic planar-distance tradeoffs face conditional lower bounds.
